#90769 25 2005-08-14T03:15:37Z stepself
Ortia - 4 - Nice and simple stuff. Excellent flow, too. It looked like it would be harder than it actually was. Can't say I liked the stacks and stacks of jump pads, but that's really minor.

Pipe Peril - a low 4 - The jumps were a lot of fun, but I think I could have figured them out without the gold trails. And the middle gauss was slightly annoying.

Pagoda - 3 - Eh. The tiles were okay, the gameplay very tough and not entirely satisfying. Those drones were used very effectively though... they always seemed to be where I wanted to go!

Turretunnels - 3.5 - Fairly good flow, but going too fast always resulted in death by rocket for me. And why did you change the gold placement pattern in that one section? It made all-gold difficult, and not flow-y. I liked how you used the squeeze-effect to force the ninja to keep his speed up.

Pyramid 51 - 3 - I really liked the top structure, with the thwumps and mines. But I don't think it was used very effectively. The bottom (the pyramid) was just a too boring. Getting the gold was fun though, and tough.

#91972 36 2005-08-17T18:52:30Z stepself
Insomnia Redux: The Return of the Erotic Mailman - 3.5 - Eh. A little spartan. You also got a NaN gold in there. I speed demo'd it before reading the description (D'oh!). It would make an interesting challenge, but not the type I personally enjoy.

4 - Squared - 3 - Not a particularily satisfying mine-jumper. I dislike jumping on those 45 degree angle tiles though, because of the frequent "stuttering" that I can't shake. To your credit, a lot of the map is optional. I was glad about that.

drunk like pinball - 4 - When it works, it works very well. Loved the flow, but I found it very veryhard to nail down. That's exactly how it should be, though.

Juxtapose - 4.5 - Wowza. Korbachev, you keep impressing me. This reminds me of a lot of loop type maps that end up being very linear races. But you've fused these loops together, giving the player so many options. Makes for some interesting runs!

For Jeffkillian - a high 3.5 - Fun little level. Getting up from the bottom part was trickier than I thought for such a simple map.

#95010 82 2005-08-29T03:38:51Z stepself
Breakneck - 3.5 - Lots of fun stuff here. Too much, in fact. You should settle on a style, rather than throw around random challenges. For instance, I really enjoyed evading the floorguards with the jumppads. You could expand that into a whole level. But I didn't like the thwumps in the bottom left corner. Too hard, because of the lag.

Thwumps Revenge:3 - A high 3.5 - Seems very similar to the other "Thwumps revenge". You should have expanded on the theme somehow. However, it's very tight and well designed. I didn't like that the loading time was as high as it was. Do you really need all that gold delay? It's not like the ninja can go anywhere anyhow, until the thwumps come down.

Mission Impossible - 2 - Eh. Sorry. Not very fun. It was a chore to do. I can't do most of the level, but none of it seems impossible, just really improbable, like you'd need a lot of luck to do it (especially the first manoeuvre). Or maybe just more patience than I have. That's not why I rated it low though. It lacked polish. I didn't like the gold-writing. I did like the trapdoor-jumping at the bottom. That was kinda fun.

Claustrophobia3 - 5 - I wish And (and Holy Trinity in general) were around NUMA more often. They came up with some fantastic maps. This one, while not particularily unique, makes excellent use of timing and tension. I mean, I look at this map and I think it'll be impossible to do, what with all the drones. But everything flows so smoothly. Instant classic.

Lucidium's "Rush Job" levels have already been rated by me (at least fours, but I don't recall), but I like the second one much more than the first. I love thwump puzzles, and this one is so simple and so challenging. I can't believe it's rated so low.

#112037 298 2005-11-03T09:10:26Z Adam Dobay
Hello everyone, I would like to ask you to rate and comment on the following two new maps of mine:

Golden Chocobo (needs 4 votes)
Dead man's curves (needs 4 votes)

And if you're not tired after that I would also really appreciate a vote or two for some of my older maps which never received a rating so I don't know how they turned out:

Temple of Sekhmet (needs 4 votes)
Apartment block D (needs 4 votes)
VariatioNs - Dog Kennel (needs 3 votes)
VariatioNs - Once more, with rockets! (needs 2 votes)


I have rated the following levels for this occasion:

00. come back...zinc... (krusch) - I gave this a 4.0 because I thought it would have a very good place inbetween a couple of easy levels in the game. The design is fine and the challenge is fun as well.

01. Bat out of hell (xenoc) - I finally gave it a 3 after pondering whether to give it a 3 or a 3.5, because the N art was good (no Z-snapping, at last, someone), but in the end there were just too many mines for such a short level. Also, it's very easy to get to the exit once you've got the switch.

02. So generic (niccus) - This got a 4 because the tileset is excellent for a first map. However I am not sure if it is actually beatable, especially the bottom right part with the many drones. The author says it is completeable but I have yet to see a completion demo.

03. Lazered (bobtheninj) - This receives a 4.5 from me, because the idea, the challenge and how it was carried out is excellent. One bad point may be that there is nothing outside of the level itself in terms of design and there is not too much gold to get. But outside of that it is a really enjoyable level and I loved playing it.

04. A Distinctive Therapy (formica) - A 5. I think I do not need to justify this rating, the level is excellent in design and flow all-round, it is not too hard but not too easy and it's just damn gorgeous.
It also made me realize what was wrong with the design of my Barcode level.

Some levels you've requested a rating for:

05. Oddity (Solarion) - The author has asked not to rate the level down because of the difficulty but unfortunately that has such a large impact on the enjoyability of the level that I cannot pass the fact that it's extremely hard. I'm not the best mine jumper by far, but dying at every second jump was quite bad. The map lost its fun quickly, and even more so because I've seen how much is left (three quarters almost). I think this should be either toned down or an easier version released.
On the positive side, the level is very precisely made, there is full use of almost every block, so it finally got a 3.5.

06. N's Ultimate Map Archive (MasterJMD) - I have rated this level a few days ago but I didn't leave a comment. Here it is now. I gave it a 4.5 because the idea was good, the letters and the outer design was used in a really good way and the level itself is a great challenge.

(From here on the comments will be shorter unfortunately as I do not have much time.)

07. A coldcut thermometer (_Sketch) - It got a 4 because the tileset is ultracool, but the level is a bit empty.

08. Reform (_Sketch) - Again a 4. The idea was good and the design okay, but it wasn't outstading.

09. The Possibilities (_Sketch) - 5. When N sat on that five tile and was pushed off by the thwump I couldn't resist laughing. This level is simply hilarious. Poor ragdoll.

10. Barbed Strangler (Andrelius) - A 4. A good simple idea and a good tileset to go with it. I may attempt a demo later, okay?

11. Fountain revised (MasterJMD) - Excellent level, many routes to take depending on what you want to do or how much gold you want to get. I didn't realize I've already voted for this yesterday, now I think it's a 4.5 rather than the 4 I gave it yesterday.

12. N lost his key! (InuyashaDuelist) - Unique tileset, various small challenges that make this fun overall. 4.5.

13. A cartoon world (InuyashaDuelist) - While the level was a good one in terms of playing it felt very very empty. No real challenge on top and there is not one ounce of gold. 3.5.

Okay, that's it for me for today, thanks if you rate my levels, bye!

#125849 521 2005-12-22T07:40:03Z Beo
Undefined: 4/5 Looks really noobish at first, but if you play you see why it's designed that way. I don't think I'll ever get that last jump short of a miracle. Try to improve the presentation, even in places that don't affect the gameplay.

Diamonds in the Rough: 4.5/5 You have a real talent for Race maps. This has a great flow, various good gameplay elements (some elaborations below,) awesome presentation and a smart-alec name, which is everything an awesome race map needs. I would have changed some of the diagonal slope tiles into curved ones, though.
Good Gameplay Elements:
- The delicate balance between the flow and death: in some places (e.g. the Rocket chamber,) you needed to balance your speed and your precision (going too fast would have caused you to run straight into the mines in the next corridor.)
- Good use of a small space to make a long race: You found plenty of ways of getting a big amount of time out of a small space (e.g. Tight map design, launchpads to reverse your direction, curved trajectorys, etc)

Dedication to Guiseppi: 4/5, I have infinite respect for people who make good jump puzzles.
Underground Run II: 4.5/5 Awesome Race map, good flow and length.
Diamond In E-sharp minor: 4/5 I love well-executed diagonal-tiled maps.
Pixelation Nation: 4.5/5 This must have taken heaps of planning of zap-drone paths and that tileset would have been confusing to work with but you pulled it off and made a great level.
Vines of Contention 2: 4.5/5 Good minefields are very hard to make, but this is awesome.
Some n-art: 4/5 Good tileset and great use of the lazer drones.
Crazy Doors: 4/5 That must have taken some time.
Infiltration: 3.5/5 It was a good concept, but you have to remember this in the future: never cluster more than 2 Gauss turrets together: don't use 9 mines when you could have used 4, and space your gold better. Still, it was a fun map.
Wavelength: 4.5/5 Awesome, brilliant, rockety genius.
Dizzy Comet: 4.5/5 You are a very very great maker of action maps.
Spider Lock: 5/5 ^^ Look above.
I'm gonna keep a closer eye on your maps from now on, Aju

Threeway Freeway: 4/5 Nice use of thwumps in a narrow hallway type map.
The Scientist: 4.5/5 Brilliant, I love the mine-thwump combo at the bottom and the tricky jumps at the top.
Threeway Disaster: 4/5 It's nice and simple and that works for and against it. Plus, nice tileset.
Fire Pillars: 4/5 Arrgh! The frustration. It's well designed but a bit too simple this time.

#126942 546 2005-12-26T00:25:12Z Beo
For SquidgY: 5/5 This was brilliant, I loved it. Original, fun tough as nails, clever, fast paced, the list goes on. I've started a favourites list thanks to this.
Pharyngitis: 3.5/5 This was a good one, but like you said, it wasn't really ready to be put on NUMA.
Manic Decompression: 4.5/5 Now this was a good action map. The tileset was good, the object placement was nail-bitingly annoying (good thing) and it was fun.
And the point of that was?: 4.5/5 This was awesome, I loved the tileset even if there were a few to many rockets for my taste. Only real problem was the door glitches (aka invisible walls.)
Laundromatic: 4.5/5 This was my personal favourite out of the maps you put on this thread, the object placement was spot-on, and I thought the amount of gold was good.
Three Rooms of Skill: 4/5 This was good and well-made despite the first glance.
Circles: 4/5 It looked nice but this has been done loads of times before.
Rugged Land: 5/5 Fun and with one of the best tilesets ever.
Raycast: 4.5/5 Great map, these tilesets are works of genius.
Thwumpist Sadism 4/5 I can't believe anyone managed to beat this. Good one, though.
Consistently Two: 4.5/5 Puzzles = Good. Jump Puzzles = Awesome. This tileset = Liek t3h l33t.
White Flag: 5/5 One of the best minefields I have ever laid my unworthy eyes on. Favourited.
Root: 5/5 Heh, looks like I spoke too soon ^^. Another brilliant stroke of genius.
US Customs: 4/5 It's a load of fun, unlike the real thing (well, customs, at least, I've never been to the US.)
Falling Acorns: 4/5 An actiony jump puzzle. Fun on a bun (or acorn.)
Percipitancy: 4.5/5 This was an awesome concept, well pulled-off.
Drone Liberty: 4.5 I was really annoyed when I saw you used this concept (not your fault) but you pulled it off way better than I could.

#177162 1711 2006-05-17T21:15:06Z Silent_witness
Quote: PapaNappa, May 17, 2006 03:45 pm
Quote: DJLO, 2006-05-17T20:26:34Z
a zappper was nand out on a switch
what does that mean?
is "nand" a typo or does that really means "not and"
When he said 'nand' he actually meant that there was an instance in the level data where an object or enemy was forced/bugged out of the level's parameters and instead shows up on the outside frame. When this happens, "NaN" will show up in the levell data, which is how people are able to fix this problem, which one does by deleting the the "NaN" bit and then reloading the level data, this time with no "NaN" instances to be found. Often times, have a "Nan" in a level does not make it unplayable, although it can, but people dislike them because it looks noobish and sloppily put together.

P.S. Dangit, Topo beat me by one minute...!
